turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me first, which your own procedure 4.2 says should have happened. I have until 4:40, so tell me who decided this, and on what basis.
Upset. Don't manage me, Hale. I asked you who decided, and I'm still waiting.
But I'm not changing the grade.
Not changing the grade. I'm writing that down, Hale. Then show me what it rests on, or I'm in the principal's office before my call.
I'm still not changing it. Keep going if you like.
Then here's a different question: did you speak to Owen before that zero went in, the way 4.1 requires? If the answer is no, the principal hears it from me today, Hale.
You can say it ten more ways. The answer is no.

The answer is no. So you never spoke to Owen and never called me, and you decided first and asked questions later; I'm writing that down exactly. That's two of your own procedures, Hale, and the principal will hear about both today unless you have something better than no.
